newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says asked for special budget for Okinawa.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says asked for special budget for Okinawa.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said in a statement on Tuesday that he had asked the finance minister to include in the national budget a provision for special expenditures to promote Okinawa's economy.

However, Hashimoto did not specify whether he meant such a provision should be included in the national budget for fiscal 1997/98 starting next April, or in a supplementary budget for this fiscal year which the government is expected to draft in the near future.

He also said the government, in cooperation with the three parties in Japan's ruling coalition, would make its utmost efforts to develop Okinawa's economy and to ensure employment to make the residents' living standards improve.
Hashimoto told a news conference that the special provision for Okinawa would total five billion yen.
He also said he had instructed Finance Minister Wataru Kubo to include the provision in the state budget as soon as possible.

Hashimoto was speaking soon after he met Okinawa prefectural governor Masahide Ota over a row between Okinawa and the central government over the heavy concentration of U.S. bases on the southern island prefecture.
